 WTA star who beat Naomi Osaka and Ons Jabeur announces retirement – ‘My body let me down’ 
 WTA star who beat Naomi Osaka and Ons Jabeur announces retirement – ‘My body let me down’
 Liam McMillen 
 16 Nov 2026 8:00 PM 
 Lesia Tsurenko serving at the 2023 Italian Open. 
 Lesia Tsurenko has confirmed her retirement from tennis after 19 years as a professional tennis player.
 The Ukrainian star earned a career ranking high of world No 23 in the 2019 season after reaching her maiden WTA 500 final at the Brisbane International.
 The 37-year-old was a consistent thorn in the side of some of the best players in the sport and she claimed victories against the likes of Ons Jabeur , Naomi Osaka , Carolina Wozniacki , and Eugenie Bouchard .
 The star confirmed the news that she would no longer play professionally with a heartfelt statement, detailing her decision and her career.

 “Thank you, tennis! I waited for some time before I felt ready to genuinely and honestly express my gratitude to tennis, because the last few years on tour broke something inside me, and I began to question my love for the sport,” she wrote.
 “But now, after some time and a lot of work on myself, I can say that I am truly grateful for everything tennis has given me: all the opportunities, all the lessons, the happy moments and, of course, all the wonderful people I met along the way, who shared this journey with me and supported me throughout my career.
 “I am sincerely grateful to everyone who believed in me when I didn’t believe in myself, to everyone who helped me and made it possible for me to compete on tour, and to those who stood by me through both the happiest and the most difficult moments.
 “At the same time, I have to admit that this is a very difficult moment for me. I didn’t fulfil my childhood dreams or achieve everything I had hoped for.
 “My body often let me down, and mentally, I wasn’t always able to cope with the challenges I faced. And I suppose I still need time to come to terms with the fact that not everything turned out the way the little girl I once was had imagined.
 “But most importantly, I now know that life without tennis is possible. It exists, and I can try to find fulfilment in other areas of life.
I used to genuinely believe that my life would come to an end the moment my career did.
 “This might sound overly dramatic to some, but that is genuinely how I felt. For many years, I had almost entirely defined myself through tennis, and I often became so consumed by it that I lost sight of who I was beyond the sport.
 “There is still a lot of work ahead of me — recovery, discovering myself and exploring the world around me. The world has turned out to be much more diverse than I once imagined. There are so many opportunities, new challenges and, I truly hope, many more happy moments ahead.
 I also know that I need to learn to value myself not only for what I have achieved, but simply for who I am. I don’t know what the next chapter of my life will look like, but for the first time in a long while, I’m curious to find out. Forever grateful.”
 It should be no real surprise that Tsurenko has decided to call it a day as she has been inactive on the WTA Tour for the entirety of the past two seasons.
 The 37-year-old last played a competitive tournament on the WTA Tour at a 125 event in Midland in November 2024.
 Nevertheless, there have been multiple moments throughout the star’s career where he has proved she is a very competitive star on her day.
 She claimed four WTA Tour titles in her career, in Istanbul, Guanghzou, and two in Acapulco.
 The star also has a Grand Slam quarterfinal to her name, having made the last eight of the US Open back in 2018.
 Tsurenko defeated the likes of Wozniacki, Katerina Siniakova , and Marketa Vondrousova in a dream run at Flushing Meadows, before she was beaten by eventual champion, Osaka.
 Elsewhere, she reached the fourth round of both Wimbledon and Roland Garros multiple times and she represented the Ukraine in the Billie Jean King Cup a total of 34 times.
 Her final Grand Slam performance was a first round defeat to Peyton Stearns at the 2024 US Open.
